subject: Model tiering + session budget sync for NovaProd integration
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@novaprod.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 02 Oct 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Model tiering + session budget sync for NovaProd integration

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our onboarding checklist I took a first pass at mapping NovaProd's expected usage into three model tiers and a session token budget so the implementation team can size instances and routing rules before dev work starts. I attached the session_profile.csv with the traffic snapshot you shared and a few derived metrics.

Key assumptions I used (please confirm):
- Median user session = 3 turns (~120 prompt tokens + 150 generated tokens per turn)
- Peak concurrent sessions today ~220, expected ramp to 600 over 8 weeks
- 85% of traffic is short-context (<=1024 tokens); 15% needs extended context up to 4096 tokens

Proposed model tiers (for routing & cost controls):
1) Fast tier — rw-fast-3b-q4: good for small prompts, <100ms generation per token, low cost. Use for quick completions and autocomplete flows.
2) Balanced tier — redwood-7b-v2: quality + throughput balance, default for chat with 1–3 turns context.
3) Long-context HQ — redwood-13b-8bit: for long-context summarization and multi-document prompts (up to 4k).

Session budgets (per user session):
- Fast tier: 1k tokens/session cap
- Balanced tier: 2.5k tokens/session cap
- Long-context: 8k tokens/session cap (use sparingly; fallback to balanced when not required)

Immediate asks:
- Elena: can you confirm median prompt length and the % of sessions that need document-level context (the 15% assumption)?
- Monica: can you prepare a draft of the resource request (reserved capacity vs burst) once Elena confirms peak concurrency?

If we lock these assumptions today, engineering can pre-provision routing policies, cache warming (prefix cache for common prompts), and a KB for quantization profiles. I also sketched an integration diagram — Grace, attaching the current DIAGRAM placeholder to align with ops.

Thanks —
Sofia
Customer Success | Redwood Inference

Attachments: session_profile.csv
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@novaprod.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 03 Oct 2025 10:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Model tiering + session budget sync for NovaProd integration

Thanks Sofia —

Good first pass. Quick clarifications from our telemetry:
- Median prompt tokens per user is closer to 95 (we measure prompt tokens not including system messages).
- Average generated tokens per turn is ~130.
- Around 12% of sessions need multi-doc context (we load up to ~3 documents, averaging ~2.6k tokens of context).
- Peak concurrent today is 220 but we have a marketing spike scheduled in 6 weeks that could push short-term peak to ~760 for 48–72 hours.

For the long-context bucket, most of those sessions are read-heavy (summaries / extraction) and can tolerate slightly higher latency. Budget-wise, the team prefers the balanced tier for day-to-day to help control spend.

I'll loop in procurement next week for contract items; for now confirm if the burst behavior (760 for a couple of days) is something Redwood can cover under burst capacity or if we need a short-term reserved quota.

—Elena
CTO, NovaProd

From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena@novaprod.com>
Date: Mon, 06 Oct 2025 11:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Model tiering + session budget sync for NovaProd integration

Nice details, thanks Elena & Sofia. I ran quick rough sizing with the updated numbers (median prompt 95 / gen 130). Summary below — these are conservative working numbers to use for provisioning; we'll tighten once we see the first week of production telemetry.

Sizing snapshot (conservative):
- Typical turn = 225 tokens.
- Typical session (3 turns) = ~675 tokens.
- Baseline steady concurrency target: 300 (accounts for normal ramp + buffer).
- Short marketing burst: 760 concurrent for 72 hours (plan for graceful degradation + fallback to smaller model for non-critical flows).

Model-instance mapping (GPU-efficient plan):
- Fast tier (rw-fast-3b-q4): 10 instances @ 24 req/s each (handles small-turn flow, autoscale to 25 instances for burst).
- Balanced tier (redwood-7b-v2): 8 instances on A100-80GB equiv with batching tuned for 32-token avg generation; autoscale to 22 for burst.
- Long-context (redwood-13b-8bit): 3 reserved instances, cold-start fallback to balanced tier if all long-context workers busy. Long-context instances use larger memory to host extended KV caches.

Cost control recommendations:
- Enforce per-session caps from Sofia's proposal and track per-route token usage in Console.
- Use prefix caching for common prompts (saves ~30% tokens on average for autocomplete-like flows).
- Route non-critical/summary jobs to balanced tier during burst (Grace to add specific routing flag: x-np-summary=false -> balanced).

Attachments: I updated the integration diagram with instance mapping and a simple fallback flow (integration_diagram.png).

Next actions:
- Sofia: confirm with Elena the acceptance of per-session caps and whether NovaProd wants automatic fallback to balanced tier during bursts (yes/no).
- Monica: once Sofia confirms, prepare an internal resource request (reserved baseline + burst policy) and draft a short SLA addendum to cover 72-hour spike behavior.

Happy to jump on a quick call if NovaProd wants to walk through routing examples.

—Grace
Engineering Programs | Redwood Inference
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@novaprod.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 06 Oct 2025 15:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Model tiering + session budget sync for NovaProd integration

Elena —

Thanks for the quick numbers, that helps a lot. Based on your confirmation:
- I'll set session caps to 1k / 2.5k / 8k for fast / balanced / long-context as a default. We can iterate if early telemetry suggests lower/higher caps.
- Grace: please proceed with the instance plan and mark long-context instances as "reserved" in the DPR so we can avoid noisy neighbor problems.
- Monica: can you draft the resource request and a one-paragraph SLA note that documents Redwood's burst coverage for 72-hour marketing spikes (indicate whether burst requires prior notice or can be auto-allowed up to 800 concurrent)?

Elena: once procurement confirms the short-term spike handling we can finalize deal routing and I will create the HubSpot note (HS-4892) with the final mapping. If helpful, we can schedule a 30-min ops walkthrough this week.

Thanks —
Sofia
Customer Success | Redwood Inference
